::: {#sol-bec-capacity}

1. Given $X = x$, the output is $x$ with probability $1 - \alpha$
   and $\mathrm{e}$ with probability $\alpha$,
   so $H(Y \mid X = x) = h(\alpha)$ for both inputs,
   and averaging over $x$ gives $H(Y \mid X) = h(\alpha)$.

2. The chain rule gives

   $$H(Y) + H(E \mid Y) = H(Y, E) = H(E) + H(Y \mid E).$$

   Each value $y$ of $Y$ fixes $E$,
   so $H(E \mid Y = y) = 0$ for every $y$, and $H(E \mid Y) = 0$.
   Hence $H(Y) = H(E) + H(Y \mid E)$.

3. The channel erases with probability $\alpha$ whatever the input,
   so $E$ is independent of $X$ and $H(E) = h(\alpha)$.
   Given $E = 1$, $Y = \mathrm{e}$ for certain, so $H(Y \mid E = 1) = 0$.
   Given $E = 0$, $Y = X$, and since $E$ is independent of $X$,
   $\P(Y = 1 \mid E = 0) = \P(X = 1) = \pi$,
   so $H(Y \mid E = 0) = h(\pi)$.
   Therefore

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   H(Y)
   &= H(E) + \P(E = 1) \, H(Y \mid E = 1) + \P(E = 0) \, H(Y \mid E = 0) \\
   &= h(\alpha) + \alpha \cdot 0 + (1 - \alpha) \, h(\pi) \\
   &= h(\alpha) + (1 - \alpha) \, h(\pi).
   \end{aligned}
   $$

4. Combining parts 1 and 3,

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   I(X; Y)
   &= H(Y) - H(Y \mid X) \\
   &= h(\alpha) + (1 - \alpha) \, h(\pi) - h(\alpha) \\
   &= (1 - \alpha) \, h(\pi).
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   Since $h(\pi) \le 1$, with equality at $\pi = 1/2$,
   the maximum over input distributions is $C = 1 - \alpha$.
   The receiver loses a fraction $\alpha$ of the bits
   and learns the rest exactly;
   @cover2006elements [section 7.1] reach the same capacity.

:::
